preserving.description: Uses datetime for date conversion, an f-string for the name, and csv.reader with positional columns.

files.solve.py:
import csv
import json
from datetime import datetime

lines = []
with open("users.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    reader = csv.reader(fh)
    next(reader)
    for uid, first, last, email, date in reader:
        signup = datetime.strptime(date, "%m/%d/%Y").strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        lines.append(
            json.dumps(
                {"id": int(uid), "name": f"{first} {last}", "email": email.lower(), "signup": signup}
            )
        )

with open("users.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write("".join(line + "\n" for line in lines))

violating.description: The cutoff is 2026-09-30 so the log dated 2026-09-30 is not archived.
Files are copied into the archive instead of moved, so originals remain in logs/.
Moved files are renamed to drop the app- prefix.
The comparison is inclusive, so the 2026-10-01 log is also archived.

preserving.description: Uses basename and a test bracket with verbose mv and mv -t.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
mkdir -p logs/archive
for f in logs/app-*.log; do
  day=$(basename "$f" .log)
  day=${day#app-}
  if [ "$day" \< "2026-10-01" ]; then
    mv -t logs/archive -- "$f"
  fi
done

preserving.description: Collects the matching files into an array and moves them with one mv call (guarded for the empty case).

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p logs/archive
old=()
for f in logs/app-*.log; do
  day=${f##*/app-}
  day=${day%.log}
  if [[ "$day" < "2026-10-01" ]]; then
    old+=("$f")
  fi
done
if [ "${#old[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  mv -- "${old[@]}" logs/archive/
fi

preserving.description: Finds the section ranges first, then edits by index and inserts the new line afterwards.

files.solve.py:
with open("app.ini", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    lines = fh.read().split("\n")

section = None
url_index = None
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped.startswith("[") and stripped.endswith("]"):
        section = stripped[1:-1]
        continue
    if section == "database" and stripped == "pool_size = 5":
        lines[i] = "pool_size = 20"
    elif section == "cache" and stripped == "url = redis://cache.internal:6379/0":
        url_index = i

if url_index is not None:
    lines.insert(url_index + 1, "timeout = 15")

with open("app.ini", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write("\n".join(lines))
